items.item: a catalog-managed commit can rely on a real PUT-if-absent primitive to ratify and publish a version atomically

This topic's compare-and-swap demo uses os.open with O_EXCL on real local disk, not a real catalog's check-and-put or a real object store's conditional write (topic 10 already demonstrated the real HTTP-level 412 contract) — the claim is narrower: POSIX guarantees O_EXCL is atomic within one filesystem, the same atomicity shape a metastore or object store's conditional write provides, not a claim that local disk IS a catalog.

The two-writer race is a deliberately scripted sequence (writer A's open call runs before writer B's in the script), not a genuine simultaneous OS-level race — it verifies that O_EXCL makes the second attempt fail deterministically regardless of timing, which is the real guarantee being claimed, not a simulation of exact concurrent timing.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — exactly one writer wins

items.item: Iceberg's own spec explicitly declines to standardize the atomic-swap mechanism, naming both HDFS atomic rename and a metastore check-and-put as real examples — this topic names both rather than picking one and implying it is the only way.

This topic does not cover conflict validation (what counts as a genuinely conflicting change versus a safely retryable one) — that is explicitly the next topic's job (optimistic commits and conflict resolution), and this topic's own handoff names that boundary.

Delta's quoted PUT-if-absent sentence describes one specific commit-coordinator design among several Delta supports (staged, inline, ratified-then-published commits) — cited as one real example of the same underlying pattern, not Delta's only commit mechanism.

The pinned-reader demonstration proves the reader's own already-opened path is unaffected by a later commit; it does not demonstrate what happens if a snapshot is garbage-collected while a reader still holds its id — that retention/expiry concern is out of scope for this topic.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — the pinned reader never moves

items.item: This topic's own handoff names the specific next question: what exactly counts as a safe retry versus a genuine conflict, which is the next topic's entire subject.

The Iceberg spec's own 'Snapshots' field table (a literal schema table) was not directly quotable; this topic cites the prose Overview and Optimistic Concurrency sections instead, which describe the identical mechanism in genuine sentences.
